subject: Economics
description: Annual Financial Statement, types of expenditure, deficit terms, key reforms

questions.stem: Article 112 of the Constitution refers to:
questions.explanation: Article 112 — Pres shall cause to be laid before Parliament the ANNUAL FINANCIAL STATEMENT (= UNION BUDGET) of estimated receipts + expenditure for the financial year. STATEMENT shows receipts + expenditure separately for: (a) CONSOLIDATED FUND OF INDIA (most receipts + spending — needs vote of Parliament for outflows); (b) PUBLIC ACCOUNT (PF, deposits — withdrawals not voted upon, but inflows tracked); (c) CONTINGENCY FUND (President's discretion for unforeseen, ~₹500 crore corpus, replenished later). FINANCIAL YEAR (FY): 1 April to 31 March. FRBM Act, 2003 — fiscal discipline. KELKAR Committee, FRBM Review (NK Singh 2017) — recommended further refinements.

Buying machinery for new factories here
Investment in PSU equity here also too

questions.explanation: TWO TYPES of govt expenditure: (1) REVENUE expenditure — RECURRING, doesn't create assets; e.g., salaries of civil servants, defence personnel; subsidies (food, fertilizer, fuel); interest on past borrowings; pensions; grants to states (most are revenue); maintenance costs. (2) CAPITAL expenditure — creates assets / reduces liabilities; e.g., infrastructure (highways, railways, bridges, ports); buying machinery; loans to states; investments in PSU equity (shares); repayment of loans. INSIGHT: high revenue exp (esp. interest + subsidies) eats into capital exp room → less infrastructure investment. India's ratio: revenue ~80% + capital ~20% (govt aims to raise capex share — recent budgets have done so). REVENUE DEFICIT = Rev. Exp − Rev. Receipts (= 'living beyond means' — usually bad).
questions.subject: Economics

questions.explanation: FOUR DEFICIT MEASURES (each tells different story): (1) FISCAL DEFICIT (FD) = Total Exp − Total Receipts excluding borrowings. (2) REVENUE DEFICIT (RD) = Rev Exp − Rev Receipts. (3) PRIMARY DEFICIT (PD) = FD − INTEREST PAYMENTS — shows the shortfall WITHOUT past-debt servicing burden; clean measure of CURRENT fiscal position. (4) EFFECTIVE REVENUE DEFICIT (ERD) = RD − grants for capital creation (introduced 2011-12). PRIMARY DEFICIT close to ZERO = govt's current spending matches current revenue (only borrowing for interest). NEGATIVE PD = primary surplus (revenue > non-interest spending) — desirable in long run for debt sustainability. India's PD has fluctuated; has worsened post-pandemic.

questions.explanation: India FY = 1 APRIL to 31 MARCH. Inherited from BRITISH COLONIAL convention (1867); aligns roughly with rabi crop harvest. Different countries: USA Oct 1-Sep 30 (federal); JAPAN + UK April 1-Mar 31 (same as India); GERMANY + most EU + CHINA + CALENDAR YEAR (Jan-Dec). DEBATE: should India shift to calendar year? Considered occasionally (Shankar Acharya Committee, 2017) — but inertia + rabi alignment + transitional cost have kept status quo. UNION BUDGET — earlier presented LAST WORKING DAY OF FEBRUARY at 5 PM (British colonial timing); from 2017 shifted to 1 February at 11 AM (allows Parliament to pass before April 1 start). Railway budget (separate since 1924) merged with Union Budget from 2017.

questions.stem: Which fund's withdrawals require VOTING by Parliament?
questions.explanation: THREE GOVT FUNDS (Articles 266, 267): (1) CONSOLIDATED FUND OF INDIA (CFI) — main fund; ALL receipts (taxes, borrowings, loans recovered) go in; ALL spending out NEEDS PARLIAMENT'S APPROVAL via APPROPRIATION + FINANCE Bills. EXCEPTIONS — 'CHARGED' expenditure (NOT voted but discussed): salary of Pres, VP, Speaker, judges, CAG, PSC chairmen; debt charges; emoluments of SC judges; pensions; sums needed to satisfy court judgements/arbitration awards. Also includes the Constitution's protected items. (2) CONTINGENCY FUND (Art 267) — President's discretion for unforeseen expenses; ~₹30,000 crore corpus (raised from ₹500 cr in 2021); replenished from CFI later by Parliament. (3) PUBLIC ACCOUNT (Art 266(2)) — money received in trust (PF, post office savings, judicial deposits, etc.) — withdrawals don't need Parliament approval.

questions.stem: When the Lok Sabha passes the Budget but new fiscal year is starting, an interim measure called VOTE ON ACCOUNT allows govt to:

options.option_text: Decide new tax rates instantly here also too
Spend up to 1/6 of estimates for 2 months till budget passes
Borrow without RBI approval for emergency here
Bypass FRBM deficit limits indefinitely here

questions.explanation: VOTE ON ACCOUNT — provision (Article 116) for govt to draw from CFI to MEET ESSENTIAL EXPENSES (salaries, ongoing programmes) for 2-3 months while full budget is being debated + passed. Usually 1/6 of estimated annual expenditure. Used: (a) when election year + outgoing govt presents only interim budget; (b) emergency. INTERIM BUDGET (or 'Vote on Account Budget') — preceding general election: outgoing govt presents one to manage finances till new govt takes over + presents full budget. Used in Feb 2024 by Modi-1 govt (since LS election in April-May 2024). Interim budget conventionally avoids major policy changes. After elections, Modi-2 presented full budget in July 2024.

questions.stem: First UNION BUDGET of independent India (Nov 1947) was presented by:
questions.explanation: R.K. SHANMUKHAM CHETTY — first Finance Minister of independent India (1947-49). Presented FIRST budget on 26 NOVEMBER 1947 (interim, for Aug 15, 1947-March 31, 1948). Resigned 1949 (over differences with Nehru on policy). FOR PYQ: MORARJI DESAI — presented 10 budgets (most by any FM). NIRMALA SITHARAMAN (since 2019) — first FULL-TIME woman FM. Indira Gandhi (briefly held FM portfolio, 1969-70) — first WOMAN to present a budget. Other notable FMs: T.T. Krishnamachari, Yashwant Sinha, Manmohan Singh (1991-96, ushered in liberalisation), P. Chidambaram, Pranab Mukherjee, Arun Jaitley. Manmohan Singh's 1991 budget = LANDMARK (LPG reforms — Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation; ended licence-permit raj).
